modern: Unidentified aqueduct on the Kırkçeşme line north of Kemerburgaz, Belgrade Forest
note: Label spans the chunk boundary. Drawn about 1.3 km north of Kemerburgaz on the Belgrade Forest branch of the Kırkçeşme line, where Mustafa III built the Ayvad Bendi (1765); the Ottoman name and the identification are guesses

modern: Kağıthane Deresi, upper course near Pirinççi (former Petnahor)
note: Curved label; named after the village PETINO-CHORI (Greek Petinochori, Ottoman Petnahor) marked further south-west
Curved label; which of the Byzantine-origin Belgrade Forest aqueducts is meant is a guess
Greek and Turkish names of the same village; the aqueduct village of the Belgrade Forest

fr: Aquéduc de Soliman ou le long Aquéduc

fr.en: Aqueduct of Suleiman or the Long Aqueduct
fr.tr: Süleyman Kemeri ya da Uzun Kemer

note: Two vertical columns: 'Aquéduc de Soliman' and 'ou le long Aquéduc'; the letter B beside it belongs to the spaced-out FORÊT DE BELGRADE. Built by Sinan for Süleyman I (1563)
